Gasoline savings resulting from the AFES are indicated throughout the EIS for each class separately and the combined savings are shown. If the agency decides after further review of the comments to the NPRM and additional analysis that one class and one standard are proper, the combined savings could be slightly greater than indicated. The class of recreational-type NPA's with off-road capability is being considered because there is substantial evidence that these vehicles cannot meet any AFES that is being considered for the other NPA's. If this is the case, then the combined savings for a one class standard would be in the same range as for the combined savings for the two classes. If, however, the recreationaltype NPA's with off-road capability can meet an AFES in the range being considered for the other NPA's, the gasoline savings for each number in the range would be from 4 percent higher at the low end of the range (17.0 mpg) to 2 percent higher at the high end on the range (18.7 mpg).
